public_rationale: The AGI Society's September 14, 2026 assessment found that published evidence did not establish GPT-6 Astra as AGI [e1]. That assessment does not establish the arrival of trustworthy, human-aligned general AI or provide a qualifying system against which to test the architectural prediction [e1].
limitations: The secondary review assesses published evidence about GPT-6 Astra; it does not prove that no qualifying system exists.
The packet lacks independent validation and sufficient architectural documentation for the same qualifying system.
Trustworthiness, alignment and the required architectural features have no precise thresholds in the claim.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: When trustworthy general AI aligned with human values comes, it will come from systems that are more structured, have more built-in knowledge, and incorporate at least some degree of explicit tools for reasoning and planning, as well as explicit knowledge, that systems like GPT lack.

statement.excerpt: Trustworthy, general artificial intelligence, aligned with human values, will come, when it does, from systems that are more structured, with more built-in knowledge, and will incorporate at least some degree of explicit tools for reasoning and planning, as well as explicit knowledge, that are lacking in systems like GPT.
statement.document_title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting … GPT-5

from_speaker: Trustworthy, general artificial intelligence, aligned with human values
explicit tools for reasoning and planning
our_interpretation: The condition is the demonstrated arrival of broadly capable, reliable AI aligned with human values. A developer's AGI declaration alone does not establish it.
The ordinary reading concerns identifiable architectural structure, represented knowledge, and reasoning and planning mechanisms beyond those in the GPT-style systems discussed in the post.
The first independently validated qualifying system would provide a practical test of this arrival forecast. The speaker did not specify a recognition procedure.
criteria.support_condition: The condition is established, and public architectural evidence shows that the qualifying system incorporates the stated additional structure, built-in and explicit knowledge, and explicit reasoning and planning tools.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The condition is established by a qualifying system whose documented architecture lacks one or more of the features claimed as necessary.
